712376.t: From συνάγω (sunágō, “to gather together”) + -ή (-ḗ), from σύν (sún, “with, together”) + ἄγω (ágō, “to lead”).

712372.t: Homeric and Old Attic ξύν (xŭ́n) and Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀱 (ku-su /⁠*ksun⁠/) point to Proto-Hellenic *ksún; further origin uncertain. The dative that this preposition governs continues the PIE comitative-instrumental.

712367.t: From σύμφωνος (sŭ́mphōnos, “agreeing in sound, harmonious”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā) and συν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + -φωνία (-phōníā, “sound”).

712345.t: From συμπότης (sŭmpótēs, “fellow drinker”) + -ιον (-ĭon), from συμπίνω (sŭmpī́nō, “to drink together”) + -της (-tēs), from συν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + πίνω (pī́nō, “to drink”).

712303.t: From σύμμετρος (sŭ́mmetros, “symmetrical”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from συν- (sŭn-, “with”) + μέτρον (métron, “measure”). By surface analysis, συν- (sŭn-, “with”) + -μετρία (-metrĭ́ā, “-metry”).

712315.t: From συμπαθής (sumpathḗs, “affected by like feelings; exerting mutual influence, interacting”) + -ια (-ia).

712382.t: From συναλλάσσω (sŭnăllắssō, “to have dealings with another”) + -μα (-ma). By surface analysis, συν- (sun-, “syn-, with”) + ἄλλαγμα (állagma, “something taken in exchange”).

712331.t: From συν- (sun-, “with, together”) + πίνω (pínō, “to drink”). Compare Ancient Greek ἀναπίνω (anapínō).

712301.t: From συν- (sun-, “with”) + the root of μάχη (mákhē, “battle”).

712368.t: From σύμφωνος (súmphōnos, adjective): as a noun, a substantivisation of its neuter forms, in elliptical use for σύμφωνον γράμμα (súmphōnon grámma, “consonant [letter]”); as an adjective, regularly declined forms.

712365.t: From συν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + φύω (phŭ́ō, “to bring forth, to produce”).

712317.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek συν- (sŭn-) Ancient Greek πάσχω (páskhō)der.

712391.t: From συναναστρέφω (sŭnănăstréphō, “to turn back together, live together”) + -ή (-ḗ).

712390.t: From συν- (sŭn-, “syn-, with-”) + ἀναστρέφω (ănăstréphō, “to turn back”).
